[[File:23 Hippeastrum striatum.jpg|thumb|''Hippeastrum striatum'', ''[[Botanical Register]]'' 1815]]

'''''Hippeastrum striatum''''', the '''striped Barbados lily''', a [[flowering]] [[perennial]] [[herbaceous]] [[bulb]]ous plant, in the family [[Amaryllidaceae]], native to the southern and eastern regions of [[Brazil]].{{sfn|WCLSPF|2016|loc=[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=278297 ''Hippeastrum striatum'']}}

==Description==
The [[flowers]], generally 2–4, are smaller than other members of the genus. The [[paraperigon]] features bristles at the throat of the [[tepal]] [[floral tube|tube]]. The perigone is about 7.6–10 cm in size and the tepal segments are 2–2.5 cm broad in their middle. Their colour is a bright red with a green keel that extends halfway up the segment. The [[stigma (botany)|stigma]] is [[:wikt:trifid|trifid]].
{{sfn|PBS|2015|loc=[http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/HippeastrumSpeciesTwo#striatum ''Hippeastrum striatum'']}}

==Taxonomy==
It was first described as ''Amaryllis striata'' Lam. by [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] in 1783. Later it was included in the genus ''Hippeastrum'' Herb. as ''Hippeastrum striatum'' (Lam.) H.E.Moore published by [[Harold Emery Moore]] in 1963.<ref name = "POWO" /><ref name = "IPNI">''Hippeastrum striatum'' (Lam.) H.E.Moore. (n.d.). International Plant Names Index. Retrieved December 6, 2024, from https://www.ipni.org/n/122839-2</ref>

==Etymology==
The name is derived from the [[Latin]] word ''striatus'' (striped).{{sfn|Griffith|2005|loc=[http://www.winternet.com/~chuckg/dictionary/dictionary.172.html striatus]}}

==Distribution==
It is native to Northeast, South, and Southeast Brazil. It has been introduced to [[Caroline Islands]] and Hawaii.<ref name = "POWO" />

==Ecology==
Produces numerous [[bulbils]] that facilitate its escape and [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalisation]] in tropical areas. It will grow from seeds in about two years.{{sfn|PBS|2015|loc=[http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/HippeastrumSpeciesTwo#striatum ''Hippeastrum striatum'']}}
